claim_en: THE LORD SPOKE TO MOSES — THE ONE FRAME OF SEVENTY VERSES; COMMAND: MY OFFERING, MY BREAD FOR MY FIRE-OFFERINGS, MY PLEASING AROMA — FOUR POSSESSIVES, THREE HAPAX FORMS; KEEP TO OFFER TO ME IN ITS APPOINTED TIME — THE PESACH'S PHRASE AT ITS THIRD SEAT, THE SIFREI'S IDENTITY. 28:1 is the only frame and the only narrative verb in 28:1-29:39 (computed on the morphology): the two chapters are the LORD's one speech, closed at 30:1 by 'and Moses said... according to all that the LORD commanded Moses'. 'My offering, My bread for My fire-offerings, My pleasing aroma' (28:2) — four first-person possessives on the altar's four nouns; 'My offering', 'for My fire-offerings', 'My pleasing aroma' each ONE seat in the Bible, 'My bread' ten (computed); the Sifrei parses them into the blood, the devoted portions, the fistfuls with the frankincense, and the libations — the Hebrew row: the showbread's dishes (142:2). 'You shall keep to offer to Me IN ITS APPOINTED TIME' — the phrase's three Torah seats are the Pesach's (9:2, 9:3) and this (computed): the Sifrei's identity of expression on a FREED term (28:9 already gives the Sabbath its lambs, so 28:2's 'in its appointed time' is free for the identity) — as the tamid overrides the Sabbath, so the Pesach (R. Yoshiyah answering R. Yonatan; the English drops the speaker, recorded); Pesachim 66a's Hillel the exam's row. The king's parable on the juxtaposition with Joshua's appointment (142:1). ONKELOS: 'My bread' → ARRANGED BREAD (the showbread's word); 'a pleasing aroma' → 'to be accepted with favor' at every one of the eleven seats (cut).
middah: I2 (the identity of expression on a freed term — 'in its appointed time' at exactly the Pesach's two seats and the tamid's one, computed; the freeing argued from 28:9's redundancy)

'Yearling lambs, unblemished, two per day, a continual burnt offering' (28:3) — 'two per day' here and Exodus 29:38 alone (computed): the Exodus tamid restated; the Sifrei: 'say to them' charges the court, and 'two per day' is read 'opposite the day' — the sun fixing the slaughter's corner, the morning lamb at one corner of the altar, the evening at another (the English and Hebrew rows name different corners — 142:3; Tamid 4:1 the exam); 'the lamb, ONE, you shall do in the morning, and the second lamb between the evenings' (28:4) — Exodus 29:39's eleven tokens with 'THE one' losing its article (computed on the tokens); the parser reads 1 and the ordinal 2; the Sifrei: 'the one lamb' — not more than one, though two verses command the tamid (142:4); 'the second' — second to the tamid, not to the Pesach; the evening's depends on the morning's unless the court erred (143:3). ONKELOS: 'between the suns' for 'between the evenings'; 'whole' for 'unblemished' (cut).

claim_en: A TENTH OF THE EPHAH OF FINE FLOUR, MIXED WITH A QUARTER HIN OF BEATEN OIL — THE MEASURE NAMED AT THE SECOND SEAT; ALL FLOURS ARE WHEAT BY THE ONE SPECIFICATION; ONKELOS CONVERTS THE EPHAH TO THREE SEAHS. 28:5 names 'the ephah' where Exodus 29:40 said 'a tenth-part' (computed); 'beaten oil' at the tamid's two seats alone (Exodus 29:40, here), the lamp's oil 'beaten' too (Exodus 27:20, Leviticus 24:2); the parser reads 1/10 and 1/4 — 4b's fraction class at a new seat. THE SIFREI: 'a tenth' — one of ten; 'fine flour' is WHEAT — Exodus 29:2 specifies wheat once and the one specification governs every unqualified 'flour' in the Torah; 'beaten' excludes oil pressed by cooking, and the menorah's the same (142:5). ONKELOS: 'one of ten in THREE SEAHS' — the ephah rendered as its three seahs, the translation's conversion layer at a new seat (cut from the shelf's bytes).
middah: I3 (the generalization from the one specified case — Exodus 29:2's 'wheat' read onto every 'flour'; the Sifrei's own argument; the ink's two seats of 'beaten oil' computed)

claim_en: THE CONTINUAL BURNT OFFERING MADE AT MOUNT SINAI — THE PARTICIPLE'S ONE SEAT, THE SINAI OLAH LIKENED TO THE TAMID; A LIBATION OF STRONG DRINK IN THE HOLY PLACE — ONE SEAT, THE WATER LIBATION'S FIRST DERIVATION; AS THE MEAL OFFERING OF THE MORNING — EXODUS 29:41 AT ITS SECOND SEAT; BEN AZZAI: THE UNIQUE NAME ON EVERY OFFERING. 'The one made at Mount Sinai' (28:6) — the feminine participle's ONE seat in the Bible (computed); the Sifrei likens Sinai's olah to the tamid for its libations, R. Yossi HaGelili only for its 'sweet savor' (143:1). 'In the holy place pour a libation of STRONG DRINK' (28:7) — 'a libation of strong drink' and 'pour' one seat each; 'strong drink' eight Torah tokens, four the wage-homograph (computed); the Sifrei: undiluted, absorbed in the altar; R. Nathan reads the doubled root 'pour a pouring' for the WATER LIBATION (143:2 — the first of the piskaot's three derivations); 'as the meal offering of the morning' (28:8) — Exodus 29:41 and here alone (computed); the Sifrei's order of the day — nothing before the morning tamid but the incense, nothing after the evening's but the incense, the Pesach and the atonement-lacking; each offering's libation WITH it; the inaugurations of the vessels; and BEN AZZAI: every offering in the Torah names the Tetragrammaton alone — in the two chapters 'to the LORD' at every offering and Elohim never (computed) — 'no eating or drinking before Him' (143:3; the English's inserted inauguration clause and the Hebrew's garbled 'table' recorded). ONKELOS: 'strong drink' → OLD WINE; 'a pleasing aroma' → to be accepted with favor (cut).

claim_en: ON THE SABBATH DAY TWO LAMBS AND TWO TENTHS — THE SABBATH'S FIRST OFFERING IN THE TORAH, LEVITICUS 23:3 HAVING GIVEN IT NONE; THE BURNT OFFERING OF THE SABBATH ON ITS SABBATH — ONE SEAT, ITS PAIR AT ISAIAH 66:23; THE SERVICE OVERRIDES THE SABBATH, FOR THE COMMUNAL. Leviticus 23:3's Sabbath is rest and a holy convocation with NO offering (computed on its tokens) — 28:9's two lambs and two tenths are the Sabbath's first offering; the parser reads 2, 2 (the construct 'two of'); 'the burnt offering of the Sabbath ON ITS SABBATH' (28:10) one seat, and the possessive pair 'its Sabbath' / 'its month' (28:14) stands together elsewhere in ONE verse, Isaiah 66:23 (computed). THE SIFREI: the Sabbath was inside 'the one lamb in the morning' and is taken OUT of its class for a stringency — the fixed musaf (the tenth middah); and the Sabbath's musaf proves the Temple service overrides the Sabbath — Leviticus 26:2's two clauses could run either way, 28:9 decides it — for COMMUNAL offerings ('in what does the passage speak?'); 'on its Sabbath' — not the eve's, not another Sabbath's: 'the day passed, its offering passed'; 'besides the continual' — the musafim between the two temidim (144:1-2). ONKELOS unfolds the possessive: 'the burnt offering of the Sabbath THAT IS DONE on the Sabbath' (cut).
middah: I10 (out of the general class for a stringency — the Sabbath's musaf; the Sifrei's own middah; the ink's absent offering at Leviticus 23:3 and the one-seat form computed)

check.note: 'on its Sabbath' — the one-seat possessive, Isaiah 66:23 its pair
